HACKATHON GUARDRAILS (non-negotiable):
- DEADLINE: 2026-10-12T18:25Z. Feature freeze 2026-10-12T06:25Z. You work on ONE task; stop when its acceptance passes.
- Read docs/DESIGN.md sections named in your task before writing code. src/types.ts is the shared contract:
  if you need a change, make it minimal and say so in your final message.
- Touch only the files your task OWNS. Never edit another task's files, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, setups/, experiments/.
- Tests: `bun test <your test path>` must pass and `bun test` (whole suite) must not regress. Never modify existing tests
  unless your task says so. Fixtures are built by scripts from real samples, never hand-invented payloads.
- Commit in small steps as work lands, message prefix "<task id>: ". Never rewrite history. Never commit secrets or .env.
- Never describe unbuilt work as done in README/docs. No numbers in docs except those generated into docs/FACTS.md.
- Use `entire graph impact --symbol <name> --json` (or `entire graph query`) before editing an existing module, if available.
- Final message: what you built, test output summary, any types.ts change, anything you could not finish.

## F03: Open a pull request safely
TASK F03 · Open a pull request safely
GOAL: Open a PR only on repos that allow it, with a dry-run mode.
OWNS: src/act/open-pr.ts, tests/open-pr.test.ts
INTERFACE: src/act/open-pr.ts function openPr(opts: { repoPath: string; branch: string; title: string; body: string; dryRun?: boolean; allowRepo: (ownerRepo: string) => boolean; run?: (cmd: string[]) => Promise<{ code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string }> }): Promise<{ opened: boolean; url?: string; command: string[]; reason?: string }>
BEHAVIOUR: Reads owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin` (https or ssh forms). If allowRepo returns false → opened false, reason
"not opted in", no command run. dryRun → returns the `gh pr create --head <branch> --title … --body-file …` command without running.
Non-zero exit → opened false with stderr as reason. Success → url parsed from stdout.
I'll start by reading the design contract sections relevant to my task and understanding the existing code structure.

### Candidate generation
- **Every candidate runs the Claude Code harness against DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint.** Pre-registration amendment 2 fixes this.
  - `setups/candidates/E.json`: `deepseek-flash`
  - `setups/candidates/F.json`: `deepseek-v4-pro`
- **The candidates are:**
  - E and F with the default rules
  - rules mutations: X's harness and model with the rules file patched from X's top failure codes, using `src/candidates/rules-lib.md`. For example:
    - F2 → "run the full test suite before you finish"
    - F1 → "never modify existing tests unless asked"
- **Traceability:** every added rule cites the failure codes it answers.

### Act
- **On our own repo:** a PR with `setups/<id>.json`, the rules file, the review summary, an evidence table, neatlogs trace links and entire.io links.
- **On other people's repos:** never unsolicited. Only for teams that opted in.

### Observability (neatlogs)
- **Trace structure:** a `WORKFLOW review` root, then `AGENT coordinator`, then `TOOL` spans (one per ingest, score, replay attempt, grade and cfo.ai write), plus a `GUARDRAIL gate` span.
- **Attributes:** `roster.setup, roster.task, roster.attempt, roster.failure_code, roster.evidence_level, roster.repo, roster.cost_usd`.
- **Session:** `identify(session_id = review_id)`.
- **Detections:**

| Detection | Fires when |
|---|---|
| D1 silent pass | The visible suite passed, but hidden acceptance or the scope guard failed |
| D2 low attribution confidence | More than 30% of a setup's lines are unmapped |
| D3 cost anomaly | Cost exceeds 3× the incumbent median |
| D4 environment flake | F6 hits the same task across ≥ 2 setups |

- **No API key:** with `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` unset, observability is a no-op with one warning.

### Book (cfo.ai)
- **Writes over the cfo.ai MCP:**
  - an **AI Workforce** department: monthly spend per setup, surviving changes, cost per surviving change, unattended %
  - a **Hire 1 engineer vs scale the promoted setup** scenario
## Architecture

- **Agent and CLI:** TypeScript on Bun (`bun:sqlite`, `bun test`).
- **Coordinator:** a tool-calling loop on DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible API (`src/llm`). See §"Models Roster itself uses".
- **Web:** Next.js in `web/`, with its own `package.json`. The prebuild step copies `reports/` into `web/public/data`.
- **Sandboxes:** local temp dirs for this repo; microVMs for public repos.

### Layout

```
src/types.ts                         shared contracts
src/ingest/ src/identity/ src/price/
src/score/ src/difficulty/ src/review/
src/sandbox/ src/replay/ src/harness/{claude,codex}.ts src/grade/ src/gate/
src/agent/ src/candidates/ src/obs/ src/cfo/ src/act/ src/forward/
src/cli.ts + src/cli/<cmd>.ts
scripts/ (run-setup.sh, ledger.ts, sumcheck.ts, facts.ts, corpus-find.ts)
reports/ (generated JSON)   docs/FACTS.md (generated)   experiments/   setups/   web/   tests/
```

### CLI

```
roster review <repo> [--observational] [--budget <usd>] [--out reports/<slug>]
roster replay <repo> --tasks plan.json
roster gate <repo>
roster act <repo> [--pr]
roster book [--org <org>]
roster forward --backlog experiments/forward-backlog.md --pair OLD,NEW --parallel 4
roster acceptance --backlog experiments/forward-backlog.md --out experiments/acceptance/
roster facts
```

### Data model (`.roster/roster.db`, exported to `reports/*.json`)
- **`sessions`:**
  - `id, repo, checkpoint_id, harness, model, rules_hash, setup_id`
  - `tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write, cost_usd, n_user_prompts`
### Security
- Public repo code runs only in microVMs.
- No secrets in prompts: session transcripts are public.
- Sandboxes get only scoped, revocable keys.
- Entire shadow branches are never pushed.

## Claims
- **Where numbers come from:** `docs/FACTS.md`, which `roster facts` generates from `reports/`. `scripts/sumcheck.ts` must pass before any number is published.
- **Wording:** "significant" only when p < 0.05. Our own runs are labelled as ours. Tests are a proxy for value, and the README says so.

# Roster: neatHack build log

## Project
- **Name:** Roster
- **One line:** an agent that runs performance reviews for your AI coding agents.
- **Problem:** teams run several coding-agent setups (harness, model, rules file). They can't see which setup's work survives and which gets reverted or rewritten, so they pick setups on feel. They also can't plan "hire an engineer, or scale the agents?" with real numbers.

## Team
- Raj Karia ([@rajkaria](https://github.com/rajkaria))

## Stack
- **Used now:** TypeScript on Bun, Claude Code.
- **Planned, not yet in use:**
  - Codex CLI, still pending installation
  - Entire for session capture, then checkpoints as Roster's input
  - neatlogs for tracing Roster's runs
  - cfo.ai for the AI-workforce line and the business plan
  - Next.js on Vercel
  - Amazon Bedrock

## Build log
- **2026-10-10 12:30 IST:** the build window opened.
- **2026-10-10 15:10–15:20 IST:** a spike on replaying a past agent task at its parent commit.
  - **Sandbox:** `git archive` held 0 of 6 future objects.
  - **Rules swap:** a permissive rules file led the agent to edit an existing test. A strict one didn't, and the grader flagged the difference.
  - **Headless CLI:** couldn't authenticate yet, so no cost was measured.
- **2026-10-10 ~18:10 IST:** repo created; skeleton, setup definitions, design contract and pre-registration committed.
- **2026-10-10 18:48 IST:** Entire enabled (branch backend, email and phone redaction on).
  - A one-line canary session (T00) confirmed that each checkpoint records the agent, the model, the token usage, the files and the setup tag.
- **2026-10-10 18:50–19:00 IST:** two privacy fixes before any session data went public.
  - **Isolated config:** setup sessions now run with their own Claude Code config directory.
  - **Worktrees moved out of `$HOME`:** Claude Code loads `<ancestor>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` for every ancestor directory, so the operator's personal rules file had been entering session transcripts.
  - Both canary checkpoints that contained it were deleted before being pushed.
- **2026-10-10 19:00 IST:** setup C switched to Claude Code + Haiku 5.5. Codex wasn't available, so the pre-registered fallback applied (`experiments/PREREGISTRATION.md`, amendment 1).
- **2026-10-10 19:00–19:10 IST:** wave 1 ran as 5 parallel recorded sessions:
  - T01 shared types and fixture builder (A)
  - T05 price table (C)
  - T09 replay sandbox (D)
  - T13 web skeleton (B)
  - T15 sumcheck and facts (B)
  - All merged with `--no-ff`. The suite passes and the typecheck is clean.

- **2026-10-10 19:10 → 2026-10-11 01:30 IST:** waves 2–4 and B2, plus integration tasks T27–T51.
  - Everything is merged with `--no-ff`, about 50 recorded agent sessions in all. The suite has 478 tests and passes.
  - The web app is live at https://roster-five-chi.vercel.app with this repo's own review.
- **Roster's review of its own repo caught its own silent mistakes.** Each was a green run with a wrong number, and each was fixed by a recorded task:
  - it saw 3 setups where there are 4 (T29, T41)
  - Haiku sessions were priced at $0 (T30, T40)
  - 16 of 23 tasks lost their hidden tests (T36, T44)
  - prompts were counted once per checkpoint (T37, T41)
  - replays failed silently when the rules file was unchanged (T38)
  - DeepSeek runs were priced with Claude prices (T43)
- **Protocol deviation:** sessions T18 and T28 ran without setup D's rules. Pre-registration amendment 4 records it and how they're analysed.
- **2026-10-10 22:40 IST:** the forward backlog (40 tasks) and its 40 acceptance tests were frozen before any review. The hashes are in `experiments/FREEZE.txt`.
- **First end-to-end replay (G4):** a past task (T12) was replayed at its parent commit under setup C and DeepSeek candidate E.
  - C passed the suite but failed the original task's hidden tests.
  - E ran out of turns at the 40-turn cap. The original session took 59, so the cap now scales with the original (T46).
  - E's cost is now priced from tokens: $0.045, against Claude Code's $2.01 estimate.

## Demo
- Pending.

## Known limitations and next steps
- Nothing is live yet.
- Every number will come from `docs/FACTS.md`, which is generated from `reports/`.

## Submission
- **Confirmed requirements:**
  - a public repo with commits made during the event
  - a demo video of 3 minutes or less covering neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai
  - a cfo.ai plan with pricing, costs, revenue and runway
  - neatlogs before/after runs with the numbers compared
  - a failed-action recovery run
  - #neatHack posts
- **Outstanding:** all of the above.

# Decision Journal

Every autonomous decision gets an entry. Two-way doors get one line; one-way
doors get the full block.

## D<N>: <title>
- **Sprint:** <n>  **Date:** <YYYY-MM-DD>

- **Chose:** <x>
- **Why:** <reasoning — user workflow first, implementation convenience last>
- **Cost to reverse:** <low/medium/high — what it would take>
-->

## 2026-10-10 18:15 IST · Product code is written only by the four recorded setups (one-way door)
- **Options:**
  - (a) the orchestrator's own subagents build everything, which is fast
  - (b) every product task runs through `scripts/run-setup.sh` under its pre-registered setup, as a separate Claude Code or Codex process captured by Entire
- **Choice:** (b).
- **Why:** this repo is the dataset Roster reviews, and the pre-registration fixes the setup assignment. Code written outside a recorded setup session would show up as human work and break the experiment.
- **Cost to reverse:** high. Anything built outside the protocol would have to be labelled as excluded.

## 2026-10-10 18:15 IST · Builds run with project-only settings
- **Decision:** `--setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config`, with a project permission allowlist in `.claude/settings.json`.
- **Why:** the kickoff spike showed that host plugins and hooks leak into every setup otherwise.
- **Reversible:** yes.

## 2026-10-10 18:15 IST · The Entire branch backend
- **Decision:** `entire/checkpoints/v1`, not hidden refs.
- **Why:** it's visible on GitHub, and `entire judge add` fetches `refs/heads/entire/*`.
- **Reader:** Roster still reads both backends.

## 2026-10-10 19:40 IST · DeepSeek for the product, Claude only for replaying the setups under review (one-way door, operator decision)
- **What the operator decided:** "don't use claude apis for the product", plus their answer to the question "DeepSeek candidates only".
- **The rule now:**
  - Roster's own LLM calls (coordinator, judge, acceptance writer) go to DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible API, traced with neatlogs `wrapOpenAI`.
  - Originals are replayed as they are, as the control.
  - Candidates run Claude Code against `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic` (E = deepseek-flash, F = deepseek-v4-pro).
- **What it costs:** that endpoint ignores `cache_control`, and its pricing depends on time of day.
- **To reverse it:** add Claude candidates back to `setups/candidates/`. The pre-registration amendment stays on the record.

## 2026-10-10 20:30 IST · SP4 closed with two items carried into SP5
- **What happened:** `roster review --observational` works end to end on this repo (17 sessions, all correctly censored as too young).
- **Carried over:** the web/CLI review shapes diverged, because they were built in parallel. The public-repo review is also outstanding.
- **Where they went:** both moved to SP5, through integration task T27 and corpus task T26.
- **Plan change:** acceptance moved; scope did not.
- 2026-10-10 21:15 IST · Reviews of any repo go to `reports/<owner>__<repo>/`, including this one (`reports/rajkaria__roster/`). `reports/self/` holds only the experiment's own files: the task ledger, the forward run and the pre-registration hash. Two-way door.
- 2026-10-11 01:54 IST · T54 (D) also edited src/harness/types.ts, which wasn't in its OWNS, to add the errorKind variant. Merged; noted as a scope deviation (F7-type) for the record.

GOAL: Render the PR description Roster opens when it promotes a setup, using only data it is given.

Rejected candidates (each with reasons), Links. Totals line "x of n tasks passed (incumbent y of n)". Never prints a number that is
not derivable from the input; no adjectives such as "significant" or "best". Empty rejected list → section says "None".

## F03: Open a pull request safely
TASK F03 · Open a pull request safely
GOAL: Open a PR only on repos that allow it, with a dry-run mode.
OWNS: src/act/open-pr.ts, tests/open-pr.test.ts
INTERFACE: src/act/open-pr.ts function openPr(opts: { repoPath: string; branch: string; title: string; body: string; dryRun?: boolean; allowRepo: (ownerRepo: string) => boolean; run?: (cmd: string[]) => Promise<{ code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string }> }): Promise<{ opened: boolean; url?: string; command: string[]; reason?: string }>
BEHAVIOUR: Reads owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin` (https or ssh forms). If allowRepo returns false → opened false, reason

INTERFACE: src/obs/detections.ts function detect(input: { replays: { task: string; setup: string; suitePass: boolean; hiddenPass: boolean; scopeOk: boolean; costUsd: number | null; failureCodes: string[] }[]; incumbent: string; unmappedLineShare: Record<string, number> }): { id: 'D1' | 'D2' | 'D3' | 'D4'; setup?: string; task?: string; detail: string }[]
